core_obligations: Choose an etale covering {U_i -> X} trivialising the sheaf (proof lines 10092-10094): this is the definition of locally constant, and it fixes the modules M_i with F|_{U_i} isomorphic to underline M_i restricted to U_i.

See that the fibre product U_i x_X U_j is empty whenever M_i and M_j are not isomorphic (proof lines 10095-10096): on a common refinement the two restrictions are both constant, and a nonempty U_i x_X U_j would force the two modules to agree.
Assemble, for each module M, the set I_M of indices with M_i isomorphic to M and the open subset U_M = union of Im(U_i -> X) (proof lines 10097-10099), using openness of etale morphisms.
Show that X is the disjoint union of the open sets U_M (proof lines 10100-10101): each U_i lies in exactly one U_M by the emptiness in the previous step, so the U_M are pairwise disjoint and cover X.
Conclude from connectedness of X that exactly one U_M is nonempty (proof lines 10101-10102), so that F is isomorphic to underline M on the whole of the chosen covering, which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: Trivialise F on an etale covering {U_i -> X}, getting F|_{U_i} = underline M_i|_{U_i}.
Note U_i x_X U_j empty whenever M_i is not isomorphic to M_j.
Group the indices by the isomorphism class of M_i and put U_M = union of the images Im(U_i -> X), open because etale morphisms are open.
The U_M form a disjoint open covering of X; connectedness leaves exactly one nonempty U_M, and the lemma follows.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a locally constant sheaf of Lambda-modules on a connected scheme X is constant on some etale covering (statement lines 10083-10089). The non-formal content is the grouping step: one must define I_M = {i | M_i is isomorphic to M}, observe that U_i x_X U_j is empty whenever M_i and M_j are not isomorphic (proof lines 10095-10096), and then use openness of etale morphisms to make U_M = union of the images Im(U_i -> X) an open subset (proof lines 10097-10099). Connectedness then forces exactly one open piece to be nonempty, which is the conclusion. The claim is H2: one explicit construction and a short connectedness argument.
